opening.argument: The video presents narrated Reddit IT-support stories, not a request for money, credentials, or a product purchase. Its description says the posts are read aloud, and the narration stays with technical anecdotes: one explains why a desktop was treated as a laptop after detecting a battery, while another describes correcting a shortcut with a preference file. Those concrete troubleshooting details support an entertainment and technology-support reading. The generic request to subscribe does not change that: it is not tied to payment, private data, promised returns, or an external benefit claim.

citations.quote: Reddit posts directly from r/TalesFromTechSupport, read aloud for your convience and pleasure
the desktop had somehow seen this battery and decided it must therefore be a laptop, since it has a battery.
The fix for this is to push a preference file that corrects where the shortcut is launching so that it runs the correct program.
